The key tasks in understanding classical Chinese include word sense disambiguation (WSD) and translation. The WSD aims to select the most fitting meaning of a polysemous word within its context. For translation, traditional methods employ encoder-decoder approaches to achieve literal translation of sentences.

We employ three categories of evaluation metrics to comprehensively assess translation quality. First, classic token-based metrics, including BLEU and ROUGE-N, focus on surface-form overlap. Second, semantic-based metrics, such as BERTScore and METEOR, evaluate the preservation of meaning and semantic similarity. Third, we use refined metrics BLEU WAS and ROUGE-N WAS , which incorporate contextual word alignment signals to better align with human judgment.

Due to the limitations of automatic metrics, we conduct a manual quality assessment in Table . We select 100 random entries and gather their real labels.
